- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing reversal.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast for 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is near recent mean, model often drifts toward extremes; apply mean-reversion bias: forecast toward 10–15% of recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates in high-sentiment periods; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment >0.67 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently bearish and price is falling, model often fails to anticipate bottoming; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment <0.33 and price is below 10-day moving average.
